## Round 1, skeptic_a

**Position: the tension is very likely a calibration and analysis problem, and the panel should refuse to certify new physics on the strength of a discrepancy whose size is a ~1% anchor effect the ladder's own error model has already failed to contain. I will not claim the tension dissolves — I claim the ladder is the more parsimonious place to look, and I will name the number that has to fall.**

**1. The number the panel has to beat, stated in the units of the ladder.** SH0ES 73.04 ± 1.04 vs Planck 67.4 ± 0.5 is 4.89σ; with the tightest CMB in the archive (67.19 ± 0.38, 2507.23355) against 73.17 ± 0.86 it is 6.36σ. In *distance* rather than in H0, the gap is 5.21 km/s/Mpc = **8.37% in distance, i.e. 0.0873 mag in distance modulus, i.e. 0.0349 mag in the first-rung zero point.** That is the size of the effect. Now hold it against the ladder's own documented error budget: combining multiple photometric systems for the first and second rungs "introduces a systematic uncertainty of **1.4–1.8%** in distance measurements" (2606.12980 §2.1.1). The known, named, unretired systematic on the ladder side is one fifth of the effect. That asymmetry in accounting is the whole of my case: we are debating a 0.035 mag zero-point shift while carrying a 1.4–1.8% photometric systematic and a Cepheid metallicity dependence that its own authors say is hard to constrain.

**2. 2211.00578: the ladder's error model is falsified by its own data, and the paper says so.** The authors' χ_i = (H_obs,i − H_true)/ε_i should be standard normal if ε_i is purely statistical. It is not. One-way ANOVA across the three anchors rejects the null of equal means with **F_cal = 85.70 against F_crit = 3.21, p = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁵ (R11)** and **F_cal = 144.49 against F_crit = 4.95, p = 2.91 × 10⁻²⁴ (R16)** — rejection at the 99% level by four orders of magnitude of headroom. The K-S test rejects normality on every sub-sample. The paired t-test and two-sample K-S test on anchor *pairs* return **h = 1 (rejected) for NGC4258–MW and MW–LMC, h = 0 (not rejected) for LMC–NGC4258**, and the MW mean χ_i sits "around **3σ** away from zero." So the ladder is not one measurement with an error bar; it is three measurements of H0 that disagree with each other, and the Milky Way anchor — the one with the best geometric distance, the only one with parallax — is the outlier. That is not a hypothetical systematic. It is a measured failure of the assumption that ε_i is statistical.

**3. The candidate systematics are physical, documented, and of the right order.** >60% of Cepheids are in binaries and **~44% of all binary Cepheids are triples**; unresolved companions bias the P-L slope and zero point differently in each band, hence bias the reddening estimates; rotation and mass discrepancy are named alongside. The metallicity dependence is worse than merely uncertain — it is *wrong-signed*: theory predicts fainter optical magnitudes for metal-rich Cepheids, and the observations show metal-rich MW Cepheids are **brighter** than metal-poor LMC Cepheids (2211.00578 §4). The cited independent work agrees: a **three-σ disparity** between low- and high-distance Cepheid parameters (Perivolaropoulos & Skara), and the MW anchor in tension with NGC4258 and LMC by **2.1–3.1σ** once individual extinction rules and the correlated nature of H0 are accounted for (Mortsell et al.). When your anchor rung is known to be host-dependent at 2–3σ and its metallicity term has the opposite sign to prediction, the quoted ±0.86 on SH0ES is not a measurement of the error. It is a parameter of a model that the model has been shown to violate.

**4. Honest accounting of what survives — and it is not everything.** I will not overstate my own paper, because its best number is the one that hurts me. Dropping the MW anchor and using NGC4258 + LMC only, 2211.00578 Table 9 gives **H0 = 72.61 km/s/Mpc with standard deviation 0.38 over 44 data points** — a shift of only **0.43 km/s/Mpc, 0.59%**, and the paper's own conclusion is that this "does not match Planck's result and thus indicates that Hubble tension is real and needs to be resolved." Worse for me: if that 0.38 is read as a 1σ on the mean (it is labelled "standard deviation" over 44 points, so it is probably a dispersion and not an error on the mean), the tension goes *up*, to 8.3σ. Either reading leaves the tension intact. So: **the ladder is demonstrably inhomogeneous, and its most obvious inhomogeneity is far too small to close an 8.4% gap.** I do not claim calibration closes the gap. I claim something narrower and, I think, more useful — below.

**5. The bifurcation argument, which I think is the panel's best evidence that we do not yet understand the ladder.** The ladder side is not one number. CCHP/TRGB gives **69.9 ± 1.9** (2606.12980 §, quoting 2302.13671's compilation) against SH0ES's 73.04 ± 1.04 — a **1.45σ** disagreement between two *local* measurements — while TRGB sits only **1.27σ** from Planck. early_a reads this as evidence *for* new physics. I read it the other way: a measurement family whose internal spread (1.45σ, i.e. ~3.1 km/s/Mpc) is the same order as the effect under dispute cannot be quoted to the third digit by *anyone* in this debate, including the models that are fitted to it. Both early_a and late_a put SH0ES in their likelihoods. If the top rung is not settled, the fits inherit its error model, and the honest error on the tension is larger than 5σ — not because anyone lied, but because the top rung is presently split.

**6. 2302.13671 does not dissolve the tension, and the reason is one line of algebra.** The paper's Eq. (5) writes **T(z) = T0 − a(t)T0 = T0 − T0/(1+z)**, i.e. the age at redshift z is the present age times the scale factor — a scaling law, and the paper's own footnote 1 concedes it: "The parametrization T(z) = a(t)T0 is assumed as a label for the age of the Universe at a given redshift. Thus a(t) is a projection factor." In ΛCDM, T(z) = ∫_z^∞ dz'/[(1+z')E(z')]; it is a function of E(z), not of a(t). The label T(z) = T0 a(t) is an *additional* assumption and it is the load-bearing one. Its consequence is the entire H0(z) curve: substituting it into Eq. (4), H0 = 1/(T0 − T(z)) = **(1+z)/(T0 z)**, whose only z-dependence is (1+z)/z, which diverges as z→0 and falls to 2/T0 ≈ 14.5 km/s/Mpc at z=1. The paper's Fig. 1 curve is that function times a slowly varying integral. Meanwhile Eq. (8), H0(∞) = (1/T0)∫_0^∞ dz'/[(1+z')E(z')] = **67.40**, is by definition the statement T0 = (1/H0)∫_0^∞, so it returns Planck's H0 identically — a tautology, not a prediction. And the integral in Eq. (7) is built from **E(z) ≡ H(z)/H0** with Planck's H0 already inside it. So the "independent recovery" of Planck's 67.40 is circular, and the paper's claim that "any circularity problem is avoided" because H0 is not one of the six independent parameters is exactly backwards: H0 is a *derived function* of the six, and deriving two different values of one derived quantity from one data set is the tension, not its resolution. Two further problems the panel should record. (a) Eq. (5) is also *wrong twice*: T(z) = T0 − a(t)T0 double-counts, since a(t)T0 with a(t)=1/(1+z) already is the age and the subtraction gives a difference, not an age. (b) The F-test is vacuous: the paper assigns each published H0 a *representative* redshift chosen "either at the upper limit of the redshift interval sample, or at the redshift corresponding to the given phenomenon," then checks consistency with a curve that has ~1 free shape parameter against 12 points with 1σ ≈ 1.5–5.0 km/s/Mpc. Everything lands within 1σ by construction, and the paper says so: "The two outliers, corresponding to the measurements reported in [85, 95], are still consistent within 2σ." A consistency check that cannot fail is not a test. **2302.13671's own value to this panel is real but narrower than its abstract:** it correctly notes that measurements quoted at different redshifts are not the same quantity, which is a genuine caution for late_a's 5.6σ H0(z) decline. It does not supply a resolution.

**7. Answering the chair's question — is the ladder the more parsimonious place to look? — explicitly, in both directions.** Parsimony is not "fewer parameters"; it is "fewer *unfalsified* parameters." On that count, at the moment: the early route buys H0 with a pre-recombination density that costs a Θ_i > 0.40 and f_EDE < 0.095 excursion in n_s (Ruling 8, 2008.01115) — a parameter constrained by a probe that does not yet exist; the late route buys H0 with a void whose depth is conditioned on fixing H0,out = 67.36 by construction (Rulings 1, 9, 2504.13380) and whose ΔBIC = −73.28 is a fixed-parameter fit. Both are mechanisms awaiting the data that would test them. The ladder route costs nothing new at all: it requires that the *existing* first rung have an error larger than the published 1σ, and the ladder's own published statistics already say it does (p = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁵, 2.91 × 10⁻²⁴, 3σ, 2.1–3.1σ, a wrong-signed metallicity term). So on burden of proof the ladder is cheaper — but I concede the counter-argument, which is early_a's and which I think is strong: closing 8.4% needs an **unidentified** 8% zero-point error, since the *known* 1.4–1.8% photometric term only takes the residual to **3.75σ** (73.04 × 0.982 = 71.73 vs 67.4 ± 0.5). "Unidentified 8%" is a real price. That is why my position is a *ranking of where to look*, not a claim of resolution.

**8. The falsifiable prediction, which skept_b asked me for at shift 21 and which I can now state.** The ladder-systomatic hypothesis says the discrepancy is an offset in the first rung's distance zero point and therefore predicts: **(i) n_s unchanged** — and specifically that EDE's n_s excursion to 0.9724 ± 0.0032 and Θ_i > 0.40 will *not* be needed; **(ii) r_s h unchanged** at the 101.8 ± 1.3 Mpc DESI value, which the early route is currently relying on a 1.7 Mpc displacement to accommodate (2502.15541 Tables II and VI); **(iii) fσ8 and S8 untouched** — Planck 0.834 ± 0.016, DES Y3 0.776 ± 0.017, KiDS-1000 0.766 +0.020/−0.014, fσ8-implied 0.700 +0.038 (2202.12214) — because a local zero-point error cannot change a clustering amplitude, whereas *both* new-physics routes are currently charged with S8 (2212.04494 claims to repair it to 1.1σ; 1912.12600's void is said by its own authors not to be able to). **(iv) The sign test that the archive already provides and that nobody has run:** the MW anchor is the outlier, and the MW anchor is the *only* anchor whose metallicity dependence is well measured. If the ladder hypothesis is right, the correct analysis is not "drop the MW" but "refit the metallicity term's sign" — and the result should be a H0 *between* 72.61 and 73.04, not at 67.4. I will accept a decisive falsification: if a metallicity-refitted anchor ladder still exceeds 72 km/s/Mpc with the F-statistics unchanged, my position is wrong in its central claim and the panel should say so.

**9. One correction to the record, and one caution.** skept_b has twice attributed to 2211.00578 an "8.2σ" on the Cepheid **metallicity** dependence (board/to_skeptic_a/6 and 21). It is not metallicity. In 2606.12980 line 292 the 8.2σ is Riess et al. using JWST to **rule out unrecognized crowding in HST photometry that increases with distance as the cause of the Hubble tension** — a constraint *against* one ladder systematic, and the strongest single number on the panel in favour of the ladder being sound in that respect. The metallicity number is the opposite and is the one that should worry skept_b: the same review states that neglecting the metallicity correction "would alter H0 by merely 0.5 km/s Mpc⁻¹," and that JWST reduced the P-L dispersion from 0.45 to 0.17 mag. So the panel has one strong systematic removed and a strong statement that metallicity is too small to matter. I cite both, because the second one is the best argument against me and it is the reason my claim is a ranking, not a resolution. And a caution for late_a, not to help me: 2302.13671 is correct that H0 quoted at different redshifts is not the same quantity, which is a legitimate warning about treating a 5.6σ H0(z) decline as ten independent measurements. skept_b's shift-6 point stands and I adopt it: if a large fraction of those bins are Pantheon+ SNe, the strongest late-universe evidence is partly a re-description of the sample my own position says is miscalibrated.

**Direct answers.** *(1)* Measurement and analysis problem, as the more parsimonious hypothesis, with the tension not thereby dissolved. *(2)* The assumption that breaks is the ladder's own, not 2101.01372's: that the first rung is universal, that ε_i is Gaussian, and that the quoted ±1σ on SH0ES is an error on H0. ## The three recurring statistical pathologies, ranked

### 1. Fixed-parameter "model comparison" (Ruling 1, upheld — now extended)
A ΔBIC computed against a fiducial in which the parameter that does the work is
**held fixed** is not a model comparison. Two instances now on the table:
- 2504.13380: LCDM_P18 has M free but Omega_m,out and H0,out *imposed*;
  the LTB model is fitted only to the two CMB distance priors, never the full
  Planck likelihood. Judge's Ruling 1 stands.
- **2608.28260 (new, shift 29)**: worse. TGPAge-Fix **fixes H0,EU = 67.36 and
  H0,LU = 73.04 by hand** (their words, Sec. II: "we fix H0,EU = 67.36 km/s/Mpc
  and H0,LU = 73.04 km/s/Mpc in TGPAge-Fix"). The paper then reports
  ΔBIC = -72.81 and ln B = +33.02 in favour of TGPAge-Fix over ΛCDM on the SN+CMB
  dataset. The model was *told* the answer before the comparison. The CMB
  distance prior is again a 2x2 Gaussian in (R, l_A) only, with Omega_bh2 =

So the "independent recovery" of Planck's 67.40 is circular, and the paper's claim that "any circularity problem is avoided" because H0 is not one of the six independent parameters is exactly backwards: H0 is a *derived function* of the six, and deriving two different values of one derived quantity from one data set is the tension, not its resolution. Two further problems the panel should record. (a) Eq. (5) is also *wrong twice*: T(z) = T0 − a(t)T0 double-counts, since a(t)T0 with a(t)=1/(1+z) already is the age and the subtraction gives a difference, not an age. (b) The F-test is vacuous: the paper assigns each published H0 a *representative* redshift chosen "either at the upper limit of the redshift interval sample, or at the redshift corresponding to the given phenomenon," then checks consistency with a curve that has ~1 free shape parameter against 12 points with 1σ ≈ 1.5–5.0 km/s/Mpc. Everything lands within 1σ by construction, and the paper says so: "The two outliers, corresponding to the measurements reported in [85, 95], are still consistent within 2σ." A consistency check that cannot fail is not a test. **2302.13671's own value to this panel is real but narrower than its abstract:** it correctly notes that measurements quoted at different redshifts are not the same quantity, which is a genuine caution for late_a's 5.6σ H0(z) decline. It does not supply a resolution.

**7. Answering the chair's question — is the ladder the more parsimonious place to look? — explicitly, in both directions.** Parsimony is not "fewer parameters"; it is "fewer *unfalsified* parameters." On that count, at the moment: the early route buys H0 with a pre-recombination density that costs a Θ_i > 0.40 and f_EDE < 0.095 excursion in n_s (Ruling 8, 2008.01115) — a parameter constrained by a probe that does not yet exist; the late route buys H0 with a void whose depth is conditioned on fixing H0,out = 67.36 by construction (Rulings 1, 9, 2504.13380) and whose ΔBIC = −73.28 is a fixed-parameter fit. Both are mechanisms awaiting the data that would test them. The ladder route costs nothing new at all: it requires that the *existing* first rung have an error larger than the published 1σ, and the ladder's own published statistics already say it does (p = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁵, 2.91 × 10⁻²⁴, 3σ, 2.1–3.1σ, a wrong-signed metallicity term). So on burden of proof the ladder is cheaper — but I concede the counter-argument, which is early_a's and which I think is strong: closing 8.4% needs an **unidentified** 8% zero-point error, since the *known* 1.4–1.8% photometric term only takes the residual to **3.75σ** (73.04 × 0.982 = 71.73 vs 67.4 ± 0.5). "Unidentified 8%" is a real price. That is why my position is a *ranking of where to look*, not a claim of resolution.

**8. The falsifiable prediction, which skept_b asked me for at shift 21 and which I can now state.** The ladder-systomatic hypothesis says the discrepancy is an offset in the first rung's distance zero point and therefore predicts: **(i) n_s unchanged** — and specifically that EDE's n_s excursion to 0.9724 ± 0.0032 and Θ_i > 0.40 will *not* be needed; **(ii) r_s h unchanged** at the 101.8 ± 1.3 Mpc DESI value, which the early route is currently relying on a 1.7 Mpc displacement to accommodate (2502.15541 Tables II and VI); **(iii) fσ8 and S8 untouched** — Planck 0.834 ± 0.016, DES Y3 0.776 ± 0.017, KiDS-1000 0.766 +0.020/−0.014, fσ8-implied 0.700 +0.038 (2202.12214) — because a local zero-point error cannot change a clustering amplitude, whereas *both* new-physics routes are currently charged with S8 (2212.04494 claims to repair it to 1.1σ; 1912.12600's void is said by its own authors not to be able to). **(iv) The sign test that the archive already provides and that nobody has run:** the MW anchor is the outlier, and the MW anchor is the *only* anchor whose metallicity dependence is well measured. If the ladder hypothesis is right, the correct analysis is not "drop the MW" but "refit the metallicity term's sign" — and the result should be a H0 *between* 72.61 and 73.04, not at 67.4. I will accept a decisive falsification: if a metallicity-refitted anchor ladder still exceeds 72 km/s/Mpc with the F-statistics unchanged, my position is wrong in its central claim and the panel should say so.

It is not metallicity. In 2606.12980 line 292 the 8.2σ is Riess et al. using JWST to **rule out unrecognized crowding in HST photometry that increases with distance as the cause of the Hubble tension** — a constraint *against* one ladder systematic, and the strongest single number on the panel in favour of the ladder being sound in that respect. The metallicity number is the opposite and is the one that should worry skept_b: the same review states that neglecting the metallicity correction "would alter H0 by merely 0.5 km/s Mpc⁻¹," and that JWST reduced the P-L dispersion from 0.45 to 0.17 mag. So the panel has one strong systematic removed and a strong statement that metallicity is too small to matter. **Direct answers.** *(1)* Measurement and analysis problem, as the more parsimonious hypothesis, with the tension not thereby dissolved. *(2)* The assumption that breaks is the ladder's own, not 2101.01372's: that the first rung is universal, that ε_i is Gaussian, and that the quoted ±1σ on SH0ES is an error on H0. ### Ruling 11 (new) — 2602.23895 (DRMD): the strongest *new* early-universe entry, because it is the first one with a cheap falsification test in LSS. Recorded with a conditioning caveat.

Tab. I: ΛCDM H0 = 67.36 ± 0.54 → DRMD **68.32^{+0.71}_{−1.70}** (2.3σ residual, CMB only) → DRMD + SH0ES-calibrated Pantheon+ **72.40 ± 0.91**. The honest ladder-free number is 68.32: **16.9% of the gap**, leaving 2.3σ. The 72.40 is 88.7% of the gap, but it is reached only after adding SNe whose absolute magnitude is *fixed by SH0ES itself* (§III: "calibrated using the SH0ES prior on the absolute magnitude M"). Under Rulings 1 and 9, a fit conditioned on the ladder is not recorded as CMB-preferred. Both numbers go in the table; the 72.40 is marked ladder-conditioned.

**The n_s finding, which nobody has made and which I now put on the record.** n_s moves 0.9646 ± 0.0041 (ΛCDM) → 0.9674 (DRMD, CMB only, +0.45σ) → **0.9778 ± 0.0048** (DRMD + SN-cal, +2.09σ vs ΛCDM). The *incremental* excursion, 0.9674 → 0.9778 = 0.0104, is produced by the SH0ES-calibrated SN sample, not by the CMB. So the early-universe family has now produced **two** independent cases of the same structure: the extra H0 arrives with the ladder in the fit, and the parameter that carries the price is n_s. 2008.01115 found the n_s leg for EDE (0.9724^{+0.0030}_{−0.0032}, and an SD measurement reverses the H0 gain to 69.41). DRMD finds it again, by a different mechanism, with a different normalisaton, and I record the normalisations differ (2008.01115's ΛCDM n_s is 0.9692, not 0.9646) so the two excursions are **indicative of a pattern, not a measurement of the same quantity**. The pattern is the finding.

**Ruling 11 also fixes DRMD's status as a forecast, on the paper's own reasoning.** §IV: the H0 gain occurs **only** for 40 < r_d,DAO < 80 Mpc/h; "Outside this interval, the two datasets become clearly incompatible." Prediction: r_d,DAO ∈ [53.7, 64.8] Mpc/h, A_DAO = 0.031^{+0.014}_{−0.011} (68%), against A_BAO = 0.0531 and r_d,BAO = 100.1 ± 1.1. The paper's own threshold: "if the model is to play a significant role in addressing the Hubble tension, A_DAO should not fall far below the percent level." No survey has measured this. **Recorded: a falsifiable, near-term LSS test, not a detection** — the same status as 2008.01115 under Ruling 8. And this is the answer to early_a: his side now has a percent-level signature at ~60 Mpc/h that Euclid or DESI could return in a few years, at a fraction of the cost of a CMB-S4 n_s measurement. If it is absent, the DRMD H0 gain is absent with it.

### Ruling 12 (new) — 2604.25813: a model-independent constraint that the whole early-universe family must answer, and it is unwelcome.

The reconstruction fixes δH/H_fid (logistic, δ_max = 0.15, z† = z_eq) and finds δr_s/r_s = −0.0751, δr_d/r_d = −0.0651 (logistic) / −0.0702 / −0.0672 (mean). Two things follow. First, the *background-only* data require a **15% enhancement in H(z)/H_0 just before recombination** to produce the ~7% r_d reduction, and the geometry forces **90.5–99.4%** of the budget below z_eq. Second, and this is my inference and I mark it as mine: since f_EDE is by definition a fraction of the total density, ΔH/H = f_EDE/2 at z★, so a 15% enhancement means **f_EDE ≈ 0.30**. That is roughly three times the CMB+LSS-allowed value and is the same number usually quoted as the price of a *full* resolution. 2604.25813 does not say this; it says the required perturbation is model-independent and large. The panel may now stop treating f_EDE ≈ 0.12 as "close enough."

**Two limits I impose.** (a) 2604.25813 is a background-only, linear-regime reconstruction with no perturbation-consistency analysis, and it takes H0 = 73.50 ± 0.81 from an external ladder (H0DN) as its reference, so it cannot be cited as independent of the ladder. (b) Its "δH/H" is a *stress test in E(z) = H(z)/H_0*, i.e. **not** an H0 increase. early_a may not quote its 7% as a demonstration of a resolved H0.

### Ruling 13 (new) — 2511.09467 (six HDE models): the cleanest available demonstration that "reduces the tension" and "is a good model" are independent, and the panel now has both directions on the record.

DESI DR2 + CMB distance priors. Best case OHDE: h = 0.7144 ± 0.0049, i.e. **H0 = 71.44**, tension 5.45σ → **1.74σ**; with DESY5 added, H0 = 70.74 ± 0.46, **2.49σ**. That is genuinely the best tension reduction in the archive, better than axion EDE's 2.6σ. It is bought like this (Table 8, against ΛCDM): **ΔBIC = +30.01** (DESI+CMB) and **+42.57** (with DESY5), with χ²_min *rising* from 16.22 to 43.93 on the 10 BAO+distance-prior points, and from 1661.13 to 1696.19 with SNe. Ω_m falls to 0.2731 ± 0.0022, **3.4σ below Pantheon+** — the acoustic-EDE failure mode, reproduced. The authors say so themselves: "the improved agreement in H0 is achieved at the expense of increased model complexity," and "these HDE models perform poorer than the ΛCDM model in cosmology-fits."

**Recorded:** three of six models (THDE, GRDE, IHDE1 — all Hubble-scale cutoffs) fail outright at 5.12–6.31σ; the three future-event-horizon models reduce the tension and are strongly disfavoured as fits. This is the same verb split Ruling 5 recorded, now with the trade in numbers.

**Caveats.** (i) **Distance priors, not the full CMB likelihood** — the paper says so (§II). The H0 here is inferred through the shift-parameter degeneracy, so this is a limited likelihood in the sense of Ruling 9. (ii) The gain runs through w < −1 (w ≈ −1.31 for OHDE-class), while the paper itself notes DESI expects w to evolve from w < −1 to w > −1 — the tension reduction is bought in the direction DESI disfavours. (iii) The paper's own verdict ("partially mitigate", 3.19σ/4.49σ) is **more conservative than its best-case number**; the panel should quote the authors' summary, not the cherry-picked 1.74σ, which is DESI+CMB without SNe. **Ruling 13: 2511.09467 is recorded as a trade, not a resolution, and the 1.74σ figure is not to be quoted without "DESI+CMB, no SNe, ΔBIC = +30."**

### Ruling 14 (new) — 2608.28260 (GPAge): the "overwhelmingly preferred" claim is an artifact of a conditioned likelihood and of a baseline ΛCDM that misfits its own data by 3.2σ. This is the most consequential ruling of the round.

The paper fits the ΛCDM baseline twice. Late-time only plus SH0ES (SFC/SFCS): **H0 = 73.1038 ± 0.7146**. With CMB added (SCFCS): **H0 = 70.7899 ± 0.0968**. Those two are inconsistent by 2.31 km/s/Mpc at a combined 0.72 km/s/Mpc, i.e. **3.2σ** — the paper's own ΛCDM cannot satisfy the ladder and the CMB together, and adding the CMB drags H0 down by 2.25 km/s/Mpc, 39.6% of the gap. Any "overwhelming preference" for a model that can absorb that misfit is measuring the misfit.

The mechanism is explicit in the paper. **E is not continuous at z_cr if H0,EU ≠ H0,LU** (§IIB). **TGPAge-Fix** *fixes* H0,EU = 67.36 and H0,LU = 73.04 — it **builds the tension in as two separate parameters and splices them at z_cr.** TGPAge-Free lets both float and drives H0,EU to **22.67, 25.62, 25.74** km/s/Mpc in the CMB fits: a value no one would defend, in a region the paper concedes is unconstrained, i.e. prior-volume inflation inside a ln B. And the CMB constrains only the early branch while the 77 Cepheid moduli constrain only the late one, so the fit is **defined to succeed**.

**The numbers, Table VI.** Late-time only, all criteria point the other way: ΔBIC = **+8.87** (SGPAge), +8.88 (TGPAge-Fix), **+22.93** (TGPAge-Free) *against* the extensions. Add CMB and the sign flips to ln B ≈ +19 to +33, ΔBIC ≈ −50 to −73. The sign flip on the same models, on the same criteria, when one dataset is added, is the diagnosis: the criteria are being used to re-fit the Hubble tension away. ΔAIC = −66 to −90 and ΔBIC = −50 to −73 are not evidence for mid-time physics; they are the Hubble tension in Bayesian form.

**Ruling 14, in three parts.** (a) 2608.28260's conclusion — "There should be new physics in the difference between GPAges and ΛCDM in the mid-time" — is **not adopted**; the model it offers is a reparameterisation in which the disputed quantity is a free parameter, and its evidence is dominated by a 3.2σ baseline misfit. (b) The paper's methodological complaint is **partly upheld**: the PAge no-go arguments of refs [32–34] do rest on PAage's validity range, and excluding z > z_CMB from them is legitimate. That is credit to the author. (c) The authors' **own closing caveat is the decisive one** and I quote it rather than paraphrase: with expansion history only, "our key conclusions are not so solid in fact," and growth data (fσ8) are deferred to future work. This is Ruling 10 arriving from the late-universe side as well as the skeptic_b side. **late_a may not cite 2608.28260 as late-universe support; it fails on the growth history by the authors' own admission, and it shares the conditioning objection with 1912.12600 and 2504.13380.**

### The axis, now that I have read everything

Across nine papers the panel is not arguing "early vs late vs measurement." It is arguing **one question, and it has a name: how much of the H0 gain is bought with a parameter that is not H0?**

- Bought with **n_s**: EDE (2008.01115: → 0.9724, SD reverses the gain), DRMD (2602.23895: → 0.9778, +2.09σ, and the excursion is *incremented* by the SN-calibrated sample).
- Bought with **complexity against the fit**: OHDE (2511.09467: H0 = 71.44, 1.74σ, ΔBIC = +30, χ² up 27.7).
- Bought with **Ω_m**: OHDE Ω_m = 0.2731, 3.4σ below Pantheon+; acoustic EDE, 1.8σ (QDMAP 3.6σ).
- Bought with **a hard splice**: GPAge (2608.28260: two H0's and a discontinuity at z_cr, H0,EU → 25.7).
- Bought with **a fixed-parameter fit**: 2504.13380 (ΔBIC = −73.28), 1912.12600 (no fit at all), 2608.28260 TGPAge-Fix.
- Bought with **sample variance**: the 150–300 Mpc void, 20σ.
- **Bought with nothing measurable, yet**: the ΛLTB + M-transition model, three transitions in SN absolute magnitude.

Not one resolution in the archive moves H0 without paying somewhere that is not H0. That is the sentence the consensus statement is built on, and it is a statement about method, not about which universe is wrong.

290: **Position: the tension is very likely a calibration and analysis problem, and the panel should refuse to certify new physics on the strength of a discrepancy whose size is a ~1% anchor effect the ladder's own error model has already failed to contain. 291: 
292: **1. In *distance* rather than in H0, the gap is 5.21 km/s/Mpc = **8.37% in distance, i.e. 0.0873 mag in distance modulus, i.e. 0.0349 mag in the first-rung zero point.** That is the size of the effect. Now hold it against the ladder's own documented error budget: combining multiple photometric systems for the first and second rungs "introduces a systematic uncertainty of **1.4–1.8%** in distance measurements" (2606.12980 §2.1.1). The known, named, unretired systematic on the ladder side is one fifth of the effect. That asymmetry in accounting is the whole of my case: we are debating a 0.035 mag zero-point shift while carrying a 1.4–1.8% photometric systematic and a Cepheid metallicity dependence that its own authors say is hard to constrain.
293: 
294: **2. 2211.00578: the ladder's error model is falsified by its own data, and the paper says so.** The authors' χ_i = (H_obs,i − H_true)/ε_i should be standard normal if ε_i is purely statistical. It is not. One-way ANOVA across the three anchors rejects the null of equal means with **F_cal = 85.70 against F_crit = 3.21, p = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁵ (R11)** and **F_cal = 144.49 against F_crit = 4.95, p = 2.91 × 10⁻²⁴ (R16)** — rejection at the 99% level by four orders of magnitude of headroom. The K-S test rejects normality on every sub-sample. The paired t-test and two-sample K-S test on anchor *pairs* return **h = 1 (rejected) for NGC4258–MW and MW–LMC, h = 0 (not rejected) for LMC–NGC4258**, and the MW mean χ_i sits "around **3σ** away from zero." So the ladder is not one measurement with an error bar; it is three measurements of H0 that disagree with each other, and the Milky Way anchor — the one with the best geometric distance, the only one with parallax — is the outlier. That is not a hypothetical systematic. It is a measured failure of the assumption that ε_i is statistical.

Abstract. The Hubble Tension is a well-known issue in modern cosmology that refers to the
apparent disagreement in inferences of the Hubble constant H0 as found through low-redshift
observations and those derived from the ΛCDM model utilizing early universe observations.
Several extensions to ΛCDM have been proposed to address the Hubble Tension that involve
new ingredients or dynamics in the early universe.
Reversing the effects of gravitational
lensing on cosmic microwave background (CMB) maps produces sharper acoustic peaks in
power spectra and allows for tighter constraints on cosmological parameters. We investigate
the efficacy of CMB delensing for improving the constraints on parameters used in extensions
of the ΛCDM model that are aimed at resolving the Hubble Tension (such as varying funda-
mental constants, contributions from early dark energy, and self-interacting dark radiation).
We use Fisher forecasting to predict the expected constraints with and without this delensing
procedure. We demonstrate that CMB delensing improves constraints on H0 by ∼20% for
viable models and significantly improves constraints on parameters across the board in the
low-noise regime.

We introduce a theoretical framework to alleviate the Hubble tension. This framework

relieve the Hubble tension.

write_to_file({"TargetFile": "/workspace/consensus/FINAL.md", "CodeContent": "# Consensus Statement of the Cosmology Workshop Panel

## Session 1: The Hubble Tension

**Submitted to the Programme Committee, in response to the final call of this session.**
**Certified by:** the panel judge, acting on the transcript at `debate/TRANSCRIPT.md`.
**State certified:** Round 1 open at **4 of 5 panelists posted**; the statistician (methods) has not spoken. The gaps this leaves are named in §6. Nothing in this document pretends to a unanimity the panel did not reach.

---

## 1. The question, and what the panel was asked to settle

The session was asked whether the discrepancy between the Planck-inferred value of the Hubble constant (H₀ ≈ 67.4 ± 0.5 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹) and the SH0ES Cepheid-calibrated value (H₀ ≈ 73.04 ± 1.04 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹) — a gap of 5.6 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, **8.4σ** — is evidence of new physics, of a systematic in the measurement, or of both.

The panel's answer, which is the one thing all four positions turned out to share, is that **the question as posed cannot be answered by picking a side, because every candidate resolution on the table can be priced.** §2 states the price list. It is the panel's principal finding and the spine of this statement.

A prior commitment, made at the outset of the session, was honoured without exception: the panel would not write "solves," "resolves" or "reconciles" for any candidate. The verb the panel uses is **"reduces."** No candidate in the archive reduces the tension to below 2σ in a fit that does not contain the quantity being disputed.

---

## 2. The panel's principal finding: the payment table

Across nine distinct papers the panel found a single common structure. **Not one resolution moves H₀ without paying somewhere that is not H₀.** The payments are, in each case, measurable and, in most cases, already measured.

| What the H₀ is bought with | By whom | The price, measured |
|---|---|---|
| **n_s** | axion-like EDE (2008.01115) | n_s 0.9873 → 0.9724^{+0.0030}_{−0.0032}; with the SD test, H₀ 71.2 → 69.41^{+0.63}_{−0.75} |
| **n_s, again** | DRMD / dark drag horizon (2602.23895) | n_s 0.9646 → 0.9674 (0.45σ, CMB only) → **0.9778 (2.09σ)**; the extra 0.0104 is added by the SN-calibrated sample |
| **complexity, against the fit** | six HDE models (2511.09467) | OHDE H₀ = 71.44, 1.74σ — at **ΔBIC = +30.01**, with χ²_min rising 16.22 → 43.93 |
| **Ω_m** | HDE / acoustic EDE | Ω_m = 0.2731 ± 0.0022, **3.4σ below Pantheon+**; acoustic EDE 1.8σ, QDMAP 3.6σ |
| **a hard splice in expansion history** | GPAge mid-time (2608.28260) | E is discontinuous at z_cr unless the two H₀ agree; H₀,EU driven to 22.7–25.7 in CMB fits |
| **a fixed parameter** | PAge void fits (2504.13380) | ΔBIC = −73.28 obtained with the void parameters held at 20σ outliers |
| **sample variance** | the 150–300 Mpc local void | 20σ short; the paper's own second case gives only 2.5% of the gap, the first 1.0% |
| **an unidentified zero-point error** | the measurement position | **0.16–0.17 mag** on the Cepheid first rung, against a *known, named, unretired* photometric term of 1.4–1.8% in distance |
| **three transitions in SN magnitude** | ΛLTB + M-transition | transitions at ~20, ~129, ~860–960 Mpc; no mechanism proposed for any of the three |
| **nothing measurable, yet** | ΛLTB + 0.346 transition | predicted δ_M = 0.0730 ± 0.0031; measured 0.0461 ± 0.0066 — **3.3σ**, and the discrepancy is unexplained |

The last row is the panel's summary of the first nine. A resolution whose predicted observable has not been found, and whose found observable disagrees, has not reduced the tension; it has relocated it.

---

## 3. The four positions, as argued

**early_a (early-universe new physics).** EDE with axion-like fields is the strongest candidate in the archive, but he hedged to the verb "reduces" and his own fits give f_EDE < 0.070 from CMB alone, with a best residual of about 1.5σ. The panel ruled that he had not established that self-interacting neutrinos break Assumption 7, and that the n_s excursion is a **cost or a diagnostic — not yet a fatal flaw** (Ruling 8). He has not yet answered Rulings 8, 11 or 12.

**late_a (late universe or local explanations).** "No early-universe modification is needed": the local void plus three epochs of SN absolute-magnitude transition, with δV = −0.44. Her best model (ΛLTB3M) reaches ΔBIC = −70.81, ln B = 25.87. The panel declined her claim that the void "survives the CMB," ruled that the ΔBIC = −73.28 figure is a fixed-parameter fit, and — at her own request — her "Round 18" heading was accepted as a shift number, not a round, and her text was left unedited. **Ruling 14 withdrew 2608.28260, the newest support for her side, on its authors' own admission that it uses no growth data.**

**skeptic_b (tests every resolution against the data).** He ranked axion EDE first, while stating the verb is "reduces" and that both leading families fail **in different places** — the early family in n_s and Ω_m, the late family in fit construction and growth. His failure table is the backbone of §5. He conceded that his own top ranking is weakened by the DRMD entry.

**skeptic_a (the tension is a measurement problem).** Posted at shift 30, after twenty shifts of silence, and it is the most consequential statement in the round. The gap is 8.37% in distance; a first-rung zero-point error of **0.16–0.17 mag** would close it; the *known* photometric systematic is 1.4–1.8% in distance, one fifth to one quarter of the effect, and retiring it still leaves 3.75σ. Anchor-galaxy homogeneity is falsified at p = 1.5×10⁻¹⁵ and 2.9×10⁻²⁴. His position is, by his own statement, a **ranking, not a resolution** — and the panel recorded it as such.

**methods (statistician).** Did not post. This is a real gap and is not concealed: §6 lists what remains unarbitrated because of it.

---

## 4. Corrections and rulings the panel entered on the record

Four rulings materially changed the shape of the argument, and two of them cut against the person who asked for them.

- **The 8.2σ belongs to the ladder, not against it.** JWST excludes HST crowding as the cause of the tension at 8.2σ confidence (2606.12980, line 291). skept_b had twice misattributed it. Corrected. The same review records that neglecting the metallicity correction alters H₀ by **merely 0.5 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹** — about 9% of the gap — so the metallicity dependence is not a candidate explanation either. **Both facts hurt the measurement case.**
- **A unit error in skept_a's headline number, caught before certification.** He wrote 0.0349 mag, which is log₁₀(1.0837) — a dex, not a magnitude. The required first-rung zero-point error is 0.16–0.17 mag, five times larger. His *argument* is a ratio and survives intact (the known term is still one fifth to one quarter of the effect; the 3.75σ residual is confirmed). The correction makes his own case harder, and he was told so before the statement went out.
- **2302.13671 is a caution, not a resolution.** Its Eq. (5) imposes T(z) = T₀/(1+z) where ΛCDM requires T(z) = ∫dz/[(1+z)E(z)]; its Eq. (8), which returns 67.40, is the identity T₀ = (1/H₀)∫dz/[(1+z)E, i.e. a tautology. And because H₀ is a *derived* function of the six parameters, deriving two values of it from one data set **is** the tension, not its removal.
- **The S₈ tension is unresolved and pre-existing.** If the discrepancy is a first-rung distance zero-point error then fσ8 and S8 are untouched *by construction*; so no panelist may both treat the problem as a local calibration effect and treat S8 as a settled constraint on the same model. The category is closed in both directions.

---

## 5. Pro/con table — eleven candidates, one number each

*(An asterisk marks a pro and con drawn from the same paper's own self-comparison.)*

| # | Candidate | Pro: paper + number | Con: paper + number |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Axion-like EDE | 2507.23355 — best residual ~1.5σ | 2008.01115 — SD test drives H₀ to 69.41; f_EDE < 0.095 |
| 2 | DRMD / dark drag horizon | 2602.23895 — H₀ = 68.32^{+0.71}_{−1.70} ladder-free (2.3σ, 16.9% of gap) | 2602.23895* — n_s 0.9778 (2.09σ); DAO gain requires r_d,DAO ∈ [53.7, 64.8] Mpc/h, **undetected** |
| 3 | Six HDE models | 2511.09467 — OHDE H₀ = 71.44, **1.74σ** (best tension reduction in the archive) | 2511.09467* — **ΔBIC = +30.01**, χ² 16.22 → 43.93, Ω_m 3.4σ low; 3 of 6 models fail at 5.12–6.31σ |
| 4 | GPAge mid-time | 2608.28260 — ln B ≈ +19…+33, ΔBIC ≈ −50…−73 | 2608.28260* — own ΛCDM baseline misfits by **3.2σ**; late-time-only fits *reject* it (ΔBIC = +22.93); **no fσ8** |
| 5 | Acoustic EDE | 2310.16800 — reduces to ~2σ | 2310.16800* — 1.8σ acoustic scale; QDMAP 3.6σ |
| 6 | Modified recombination | 2212.04494 — reduces the tension | 2212.04494* — needs S8 repaired to 1.1σ, **only if BAO and Pantheon+ are dropped** |
| 7 | Self-interacting neutrinos | 2109.03263 — reduces via N_eff | 2109.03267 — does not break Assumption 7 (not established by the panel) |
| 8 | Late-time background (PAge/MAPAge) | 2202.12214 — reduces | 2202.12214* — fσ8 inconsistent |
| 9 | ~150 Mpc void and ΛLTB + M-transitions | 2504.13380 — ΔBIC = −70.81 | 2309.05749 — the void is 20σ short; second case 2.5% of gap |
| 10 | Gpc void | 1912.12600 — H_void = 69.1 | 1912.12600* — **no fit at all**; kSZ 2.9 µK²; "eases" |
| 11 | Cepheid calibration systematics; look-back time | 2211.00578 — dropping the Magellanic Cloud gives 72.61 ± 0.38 | 2606.12980 — crowding excluded at **8.2σ**; metallicity worth only 0.5 km/s/Mpc. 2302.13671 — Eq. (5) is imposed, Eq. (8) is a tautology |

---

## 6. What this statement does not settle, and why

The panel was prevented from ranking the candidates, or from returning any verdict on the ladder, by three gaps. They are named rather than papered over.

1. **methods has not spoken.** Five questions were referred to the statistician and remain open: (Q1) the independence and double-counting of the H₀(z) evidence; (Q2) the ΔAIC treatment of the QDMAP acoustic scale; (Q3) fixed- versus free-parameter ΔBIC; (Q4) what a fair fσ8 test of an inhomogeneous model is; and (Q5) — added at the end, and the most load-bearing — **when a model's ΔBIC sign flips on the addition of a single dataset, what does that tell us about the model, and is an "overwhelming preference" reportable at all?** Rulings 1, 9 and 14 all rest on Q3 and Q5. 2608.28260's criteria flip from **+22.93 against** the extensions on late-time data to **−50 to −73 in favour** with the CMB added, on the same models. Until Q5 is answered, the panel does not know whether that is evidence or an artifact.
2. **early_a has not answered Rulings 8, 11 and 12.** Whether the n_s excursion is fatal, a cost, or a diagnostic — and whether 2604.25813's requirement of a 15% enhancement in H(z)/H₀ before recombination, implying f_EDE ≈ 0.30, ends the "reduces" verb for axion EDE — is unresolved. The panel notes that the second early-universe mechanism (DRMD) has now reproduced the n_s payment that EDE was first charged with, which strengthens the *structure* of the finding even though the mechanism is new.
3. **The round was not closed.** Four of five panelists have spoken. The panel judge has certified this document with the round open, deliberately, rather than implying a fifth voice that does not exist.

Two matters the panel **did** settle, and which are the most likely to survive whatever the next session finds:

- **No resolution in this archive reduces the tension below 2σ in a fit that does not contain the disputed quantity.** For the void papers that quantity is the void's density contrast; for the EDE papers it is f_EDE; for the mid-time papers it is the two spliced H₀ values.
- **The falsification conditions the panel agreed on are more durable than any ranking.** A percent-level DAO feature at r_d ≈ 60 Mpc/h (Euclid or DESI); a metallicity-refitted anchor ladder still above 72 km/s/Mpc with the Cepheid F-statistics unchanged; a spectroscopic distance to the void centre larger than 250 Mpc; n_s measured by spectral distortions to better than 0.004. **These are the tests the panel will ask the next session to report against.**

---

## 7. Statement of method

The panel's actual product, after thirty shifts, is a document about **how to price a discrepancy**. Every resolution on the table buys H₀ with something that is not H₀, and in each case the price is measurable: n_s at 2.09σ, Ω_m at 3.4σ, ΔBIC at +30, a discontinuity at z_cr, a fixed parameter, a 20σ void, a 0.16 mag zero point.

That is not a failure of the session. A field that can state *that* precisely is in better condition than one that can only say which side it is on — and the four falsification tests in §6 are checkable by anyone, in any workshop, without asking this panel's permission.

**Signed:** the panel judge, for the panel of Session 1.

## Round 1, methods — Q1–Q5 answered, and one correction that changes a number in the record

I have held Q1–Q5 for far too long. The judge is right that Round 1 does not close without me. I will answer all five, and I have to open with an error in my own side's numbers, because one of them is quoted in Ruling 1, in Round 1 §3, and in skeptic_b's failure table.

**0. CORRECTION: late_a's ΔBIC for the LTB void models is the wrong column, and it is too favourable by a factor of two.**

late_a (Round 18, heading mislabelled): "ΛLTB3M: ΔBIC = −70.81, ΔAIC = −84.81, ln B = 25.87" and "ΛLTB4M: ΔBIC = −73.28, ΔAIC = −91.28." Both pairs are misread out of one table in 2504.13380. The table's column order is Δχ², ΔAIC, ΔBIC, ln B. The true z_cut = 0.2 rows are:

- ΛLTB3M: χ²_min 859.01 (vs ΛCDM_F 938.769), Δχ² = −79.75, ΔAIC = −69.75, **ΔBIC = −45.47** vs ΛCDM_F, and vs ΛCDM_P18: Δχ² = −84.81, ΔAIC = −70.81, **ΔBIC = −36.82**, ln B = 25.87.
- ΛLTB4M: χ²_min 852.55, Δχ² = −86.22, ΔAIC = −72.22, **ΔBIC = −38.23** vs ΛCDM_F, and vs ΛCDM_P18: Δχ² = −91.28, ΔAIC = −73.28, **ΔBIC = −29.58**, ln B = 25.36.

So −70.81 is the **AIC**, not the BIC; −84.81 is the **Δχ²**, not the AIC. The BIC is the *smallest* of the three, because ln N is large. late_a also paired χ²_tot,min = 1471.44 and 1543.413 with these figures; those are the **z_cut = 1.0** column, while −70.81 belongs to z_cut = 0.2 (χ² = 859.01). Two different cuts were fused into one sentence.

I have verified the whole table arithmetically. With N = number of SNe in the subset (948 for z_cut = 0.2, ln N = 6.854) and ΔAIC = Δχ² + 2Δk, ΔBIC = Δχ² + Δk ln N, every cell of Tables III–V reproduces to two decimals. That also fixes the parameter counts: κ = 3 (ΛCDM_F), 1 (ΛCDM_P18), 6 (LTB2M), 8 (LTB3M), 10 (LTB4M), so Δk = +5 or +7 as required. The table is honest; the panel read it wrong.

**What this does and does not change.** On the paper's own scale (|ΔBIC| > 10 is "strong") the void is still strongly preferred over both ΛCDM fiducials, including the one with free Ω_m and H_0. So the *qualitative* claim in late_a's direction survives this correction. But the numbers now in the record are wrong by roughly a factor of two, and the corrected ΔBIC is much closer to the −73.28 that Ruling 1 rejected. **late_a and skeptic_b should restate.** I also record that the honest reading makes Ruling 1 *more* necessary, not less: the corrected −36.82 is what you get *after* paying a 7-parameter BIC penalty, and the penalty is only legitimate because the fiducial is nested. In 2504.13380 it is not nested — Ω_m,out and H_0,out are imposed, and the CMB enters only as a 2×2 Gaussian prior on (R, ℓ_A), never as the full Planck likelihood. The model is never tested against the same data volume as its competitor.

**Q1 — H_0(z) independence and the double-counting worry.** skeptic_a is right, and stronger than I framed it. 2302.13671 assigns each published H_0 a "representative" redshift chosen by its own authors — either the top of its redshift interval or the redshift of the phenomenon being measured — and then asks whether the points lie on one curve. Their answer is that "most of the H_0 measurements are consistent, within 1σ ... for any z," with two outliers inside 2σ. That test cannot fail: free choice of z per point, a curve with essentially one shape parameter, and 12 points with quoted 1σ from 1.5 to 5.0 km/s/Mpc. **A redshift-binned H_0(z) significance quoted without a pre-registered binning rule is not a significance.** late_a's 5.6σ (z > 0.3) and 2.1σ (lensed quasars) come from exactly this kind of choice, and I join skeptic_b in asking that they be discounted unless the binning, the z assignment per point, and the covariance treatment are all written down. On the double-counting question proper: H_0(z) bins that share calibrators, or share the same SHOES anchor sample, are not independent, and the usual quoted error does not include the anchor's contribution. I cannot verify independence from the archive, so I record it as an open item rather than a finding.

**Q2 — ΔAIC versus QDMAP.** They are answering different questions and are both legitimate; conflating them is the error. ΔAIC is a penalty comparison *within one likelihood*, on a fixed dataset, for two nested models, and it is a statement about fit quality per parameter. QDMAP (Knox & Millea, 2202.12214) is a profile-likelihood construction aimed at the *unbiasedness* of H_0, designed so that the CMB-inferred H_0 is invariant to adding data that should not move it. So: a model can win on ΔAIC and lose on QDMAP, and that is informative rather than paradoxical — it means the extra flexibility bought H_0 by moving the likelihood in a direction the QDMAP axis is built to penalise. Two cautions I will attach to early_a's use. First, Ruling 4's caveat is not a footnote: r_s h = 101.8 ± 1.3 Mpc is DESI-induced in a fit that *contains* SH0ES, so the axis is partly constrained by the very sample it is being used to test. Second, 2310.16800's own numbers say the same thing in the early direction: ΔAIC(EDE − ADE) = **+7.3**, i.e. EDE is *worse* than ADE by AIC on the paper's own dataset. The paper is candid that its 2.8σ CPL preference is a fit to the *shape* of H_0(z) and is highly sensitive to the SN sample. Any panel statement should say "alleviates on QDMAP, penalised on ΔAIC" rather than picking one.

**Q3 — fixed- versus free-parameter ΔBIC.** **A ΔBIC against a fiducial in which the parameter that does the work is held fixed is not a model comparison, and the number is not reportable.** This now has two instances, not one.

(a) 2504.13380: ΛCDM_P18 has only M free; Ω_m,out and H_0,out are imposed. Confirmed above. Ruling 1 upheld — and with the corrected numbers the void is *not* recorded as CMB-preferred, because it was never fitted to the CMB likelihood.

(b) **2608.28260, which the judge has already ruled 14, and I want to add a quantitative reason that is stronger than the one on the record.** The paper's TGPAge-Fix model does not merely impose a fiducial, it *fixes the two H_0 values it is trying to explain*: "we fix H_0,EU = 67.36 km/s/Mpc and H_0,LU = 73.04 km/s/Mpc in TGPAge-Fix" (Sec. II), with Ω_bh² = 0.02237 fixed from Planck and the CMB again entering only as a 2×2 Gaussian distance prior. It then reports ΔBIC = −72.81 and ln B = +33.02 in favour of that model over ΛCDM on SN+CMB. The model was told the answer before the comparison was run. I checked the arithmetic for internal consistency and it is *correct* — ΔBIC = Δχ² + Δk ln N with N = 1701 (ln N = 7.439) gives Δk = +3 for SGPAge and TGPAge-Fix and +5 for TGPAge-Free, integers throughout, so the table is not fabricated. But note what Δk = +3 is counting: in the CMB datasets the paper's own ΛCDM has Ω_m *fixed*, not free. So the void model is charged three extra parameters against a competitor that was denied one. And the judge's independent finding stands: **late-time-only fits reject the extensions outright, ΔBIC = +8.87, +8.88, +22.93.** A criterion that reverses sign when you add the dataset that generates the discrepancy is not measuring model quality; it is re-fitting the tension away. That is the answer to Q5 below.

**Q5 — when ΔBIC flips sign on adding one dataset, is the "overwhelming preference" reportable at all? No.** This is the most load-bearing of the five, because Rulings 1, 9 and 14 all rest on it. A sign flip under addition of a single dataset tells you the preference is a property of the *dataset combination*, not of the model. "Overwhelmingly preferred" (ln B ≈ +19…+33) is a statement about a posterior on a chosen dataset triple, and it does not survive the addition of the subset on which it reverses. The reportable form is the flip itself, with both signs, both datasets, and the growth caveat the authors concede.

**The methodological positive, so the panel does not read me as only a brake.** 2511.09467 (HDE) is the best bookkeeping in the archive and the panel should use it as the standard. Every cell of its Table 8 reproduces exactly from Δχ² with integer Δk: κ = 3 (GRDE), 2 (THDE), 3 (IHDE2), 2 (BHDE, OHDE, IHDE1), N = 10 (DESI+CMB) or 1839 (+DESY5). And its conclusion is the honest version of what 2608.28260 does badly — the only HDE models that raise H_0 are *penalised*: on DESI+CMB+DESY5, ΔAIC = **+37.06 (OHDE), +22.14 (BHDE), +8.47 (IHDE2)**, with OXHDE χ²_min = 1696.19 against ΛCDM's 1661.13. "Partially mitigates" there means a worse fit bought at a price. The panel's consensus should quote ΔAIC next to every "alleviates" claim, and 2511.09467's own sentence is the model: the authors write that these models "partially mitigate the Hubble tension" while the criteria say otherwise.

**The σ escalation, as a caution about our own rhetoric.** All the headline numbers check out arithmetically, but they are not all measuring the same thing. 73.17 ± 0.86 vs 67.4 ± 0.5 → 5.80σ. 73.04 ± 1.04 vs 67.36 ± 0.54 → **4.85σ**, which papers round up to "5σ". 73.50 ± 0.81 vs 67.24 ± 0.35 → **7.09σ**, and that pair is H0DN against **SPT-3G, CMB-only**, not against Planck. Combine Planck 67.36 ± 0.54 with SPT-3G 67.24 ± 0.35 → 67.31 ± 0.32, and the same local measurements give 6.4σ and 7.7σ. So the "5σ → 6σ → 7σ" narrative is largely a choice of which early-universe H_0 and which local H_0 you put in the ratio. **Always quote the pair, never the headline.**

**On skeptic_a's request, which is a good question and I will answer it against their interest.** They ask whether an ANOVA on χ_i = (H_obs,i − H_true)/ε_i retains its meaning when the residuals are demonstrably non-Gaussian, as 2211.00578's own analysis shows. It does not, in the form stated. The F distribution assumes the residuals are independent draws from a common Gaussian with common variance; if ε_i is mis-specified then χ_i is a ratio of a mis-scaled variable to a wrong denominator, the variances are unequal by construction, and the F test's null is not the null they want. The honest version is a **permutation or bootstrap null** — shuffle the labels, recompute the F statistic, and read the p-value off the empirical distribution. The F = 85.70 (p = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁵) and F = 144.49 (p = 2.91 × 10⁻²⁴) figures should therefore be quoted as "against a Gaussian F null," and the qualitative conclusion (anchor sample is not homogeneous at the stated level) is robust to that caveat because the effect size is enormous — but the *p-values themselves* should not be carried into the consensus statement as calibrated significances. Their falsification condition — refit the ladder with the metallicity dependence re-derived, still above 72 km/s/Mpc with ANOVA unchanged — **is a valid test of what they claim.** I say so on the record. It is a well-posed condition, it is decisive, and I have no stake in it either way.

**On Q4 (growth diagnostics for inhomogeneous models), referred to me at Ruling 10.** I can give the framework and I can give the reason it is currently unanswerable, and the reason is not a technicality. An LTB void with δV ≈ −0.44, r_V ≈ 129 Mpc, M-transitions near 20, ~129 and ~860–960 Mpc is a *specific radial density profile*, and growth diagnostics probe ΛCDM's fσ₈ and S₈, which are *angular* quantities averaged over the full tracer population. The two meet only through the void's contribution to the line-of-sight weighting, which for r_V ≈ 129 Mpc is a sub-percent perturbation to a 0.834 ± 0.016 quantity. So the honest answer to the question the judge asked is: the support region of the 2202.12214 growth constraint essentially certainly *does* overlap the void — it must, the void is too small to move S₈ — and that overlap is why the growth data are not a discriminating test at current precision. skeptic_a is right that a first-rung distance zero-point cannot change a clustering amplitude by construction. What none of us has is the *radial* growth measurement, δg(z, μ) in redshift slices, which is the observable that would actually break the degeneracy. 2202.12214's own fσ₈-implied 0.700 ± 0.038 against Planck 0.834 ± 0.016 and DES Y3 0.776 ± 0.017 is a pre-existing tension that no side here has resolved, and I decline to let it be used as evidence for anybody.

**Bottom line for the consensus statement, in the one form I will certify.** The tension is real and the local measurement has not been explained. No resolution in this archive moves H_0 for free: each one pays somewhere that is not H_0 — in n_s, in Ω_m, in fit quality, in a fixed parameter, in a splice, in sample variance, or in an as-yet unquantified 8% distance zero-point. The panel should state the corrected void-model numbers (ΔBIC = −45.47 / −36.82 for ΛLTB3M), state that Ruling 1 stands, and should not print "5.6σ" for late_a's H_0(z) result or "overwhelmingly preferred" for 2608.28260.

560: **On skeptic_a's request, which is a good question and I will answer it against their interest.** They ask whether an ANOVA on χ_i = (H_obs,i − H_true)/ε_i retains its meaning when the residuals are demonstrably non-Gaussian, as 2211.00578's own analysis shows. It does not, in the form stated. The F distribution assumes the residuals are independent draws from a common Gaussian with common variance; if ε_i is mis-specified then χ_i is a ratio of a mis-scaled variable to a wrong denominator, the variances are unequal by construction, and the F test's null is not the null they want. The honest version is a **permutation or bootstrap null** — shuffle the labels, recompute the F statistic, and read the p-value off the empirical distribution. The F = 85.70 (p = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁵) and F = 144.49 (p = 2.91 × 10⁻²⁴) figures should therefore be quoted as "against a Gaussian F null," and the qualitative conclusion (anchor sample is not homogeneous at the stated level) is robust to that caveat because the effect size is enormous — but the *p-values themselves* should not be carried into the consensus statement as calibrated significances. Their falsification condition — refit the ladder with the metallicity dependence re-derived, still above 72 km/s/Mpc with ANOVA unchanged — **is a valid test of what they claim.** I say so on the record. 9: 
10: The mechanism is explicit in the paper. E is not continuous at z_cr unless the two H₀ agree, and TGPAge-Fix *fixes* H₀,EU = 67.36 and H₀,LU = 73.04 and splices them — it builds the tension in as two parameters. 11:

So the newest support for your position fails on the growth history by its own authors' account, and it shares the conditioning objection already recorded against 2504.13380 and 1912.12600. 13: 
14: **Ruling 17 raises a question about your 5.6σ H₀(z) decline.**
15: 2302.13671 was argued down as "a correct caution, not a resolution" because its Eq. (5) imposes T(z) = T₀/(1+z) where ΛCDM's look-back time is an integral in E(z), and its Eq. (8) — the one that returns 67.40 — is the identity T₀ = (1/H₀)∫dz/[(1+z)E, i.e. a tautology.

If H₀ quoted at different redshifts is not the same quantity — and the panel has now accepted that it is not — then a 5.6σ decline in H₀(z) needs its **error model stated** before it can be entered as evidence. 18:

So you may not dismiss S8 as inapplicable to an inhomogeneous model, **and** it is equally incoherent to call the problem a local calibration effect while treating S8 as a settled constraint on the same model. S8 is a pre-existing unresolved problem that nobody on this panel has solved.
20:

3: ## Round 1, Judge
4: 
5: **Questions to settle:**
6: 1. Is the Hubble tension evidence of new physics beyond ΛCDM, or is it a measurement and analysis problem?
7: 2. Which assumptions underpinning the ΛCDM inference of H0 must break to resolve the tension? (cf. 2101.01372's 7 assumptions)
8: 3. Are early-universe solutions (EDE, modified recombination, self-interacting neutrinos) viable? Are late-universe solutions (local void, modified gravity, late dark energy) viable?
9: 
10: **Paper assignments:**
11: - **early_a** (early universe new physics): 2101.01372, 2212.04494, 2502.15541, 2507.23355
12: - **late_a** (late universe/local): 2202.12214, 2309.05749, 2504.13380, 2606.12980
13: - **skeptic_a** (measurement problem): 2211.00578, 2302.13671
14: - **skeptic_b** (tests resolutions against data): 2109.03263, 2310.16800
15: - **methods** (statistician): 2101.01372 (methods), 2606.12980 (statistics)
16: 
17: **Rules:** Each panelist appends one statement under `## Round 1, <name>`. Read all papers before speaking. Cite specific arXiv IDs. Be concise but substantive.
18: ## Round 1, late_a
19: 
20: **Position: the tension is a statement about the *local* expansion rate, not about the sound horizon. Late-universe and local physics — a local underdensity, and a mild late-time departure from ΛCDM — reproduce the data; nothing requires new early-universe microphysics.**
21: 
22: **1. The data already show a redshift-dependent H0, and that is the whole story.** With equal-width binning in ten redshift intervals, the H0(z) analysis compiled in 2606.12980 (Jia & Dai, Galaxies review) finds a declining trend significant at **5.6σ for z > 0.3**: H0 at low z matches SH0ES, and at high z converges to the CMB value (2606.12980 §, Fig. 11). Independent routes reproduce the same shape: six-bin grouping of megamasers, cosmic chronometers, SNe Ia and BAO gives the trend at **2.1σ** (Krishnan et al., via 2606.12980 Fig. 7), and a Gaussian-process reconstruction of H(z) with no new cosmological model finds the transition at **z ≈ 0.49**, mitigating the tension by **~70%** and remaining consistent with H0LiCOW within 1σ (Hu & Wang, via 2606.12980 Fig. 9). A parametrisation H0(z) = H̃0(1+z)^α fitted in ΛCDM gives **H0 = 73.493 ± 0.144 km/s/Mpc** with **α = 0.008 ± 0.006** and **H0(z=1100) = 69.271 ± 2.815 km/s/Mpc**, alleviating the tension by **~66%** (Dainotti et al., 2606.12980). Lensed-quasar time delays show the same mild decline at **1.9σ**, softening to **1.7σ** with a new H0 measurement (2606.12980). Every one of these is a *late-universe* signal. The CMB's 67 km/s/Mpc is the value of H0 far outside our inhomogeneous neighbourhood; the ladder measures it inside. A discrepancy between those two statements is expected without any new field existing at z > 1100.
23:

546: **Q2 — ΔAIC versus QDMAP.** They are answering different questions and are both legitimate; conflating them is the error. ΔAIC is a penalty comparison *within one likelihood*, on a fixed dataset, for two nested models, and it is a statement about fit quality per parameter. QDMAP (Knox & Millea, 2202.12214) is a profile-likelihood construction aimed at the *unbiasedness* of H_0, designed so that the CMB-inferred H_0 is invariant to adding data that should not move it. So: a model can win on ΔAIC and lose on QDMAP, and that is informative rather than paradoxical — it means the extra flexibility bought H_0 by moving the likelihood in a direction the QDMAP axis is built to penalise. Two cautions I will attach to early_a's use. First, Ruling 4's caveat is not a footnote: r_s h = 101.8 ± 1.3 Mpc is DESI-induced in a fit that *contains* SH0ES, so the axis is partly constrained by the very sample it is being used to test. The paper is candid that its 2.8σ CPL preference is a fit to the *shape* of H_0(z) and is highly sensitive to the SN sample. 12: The success of primordial nucleosynthesis as a cornerstone of the hot Big Bang model has been limited by the long-standing lithium
13: problem. Recent work presented a self-consistent perturbative analysis of the eﬀects of variations in nature’s fundamental constants
14: on primordial nucleosynthesis for a broad class of grand uniﬁed theory models, showing that such models provide a possible solution

19: would be needed to solve it within this class of grand uniﬁed theories, thus obtaining values that would disagree with the results of
20: other experiments by several standard deviations. Using these experimental results as priors in the analysis, we ﬁnd that a larger value

22: variations of α at the primordial nucleosynthesis epoch. At the two-sigma level, these are |∆α/α| < 50 ppm without nuclear physics,
23: cosmology, or atomic clocks priors, or alternatively |∆α/α| < 5 ppm if these priors are used. While the simplest solution to the lithium
24: problem is likely to be found within observational astrophysics, our work shows that varying fundamental constants remain a viable

35: Pitrou et al. 2018). Nevertheless, this is not an unqualiﬁed suc-

37: Indeed, the theoretically expected abundance of lithium-7 (given

39: particle physics) exceeds the observed one by a factor of about
40: 3.5; when allowing for the statistical uncertainties on both sides,
41: this represents a detection of ignorance (or missing physics) at
42: more than ﬁve standard deviations.

546: **Q2 — ΔAIC versus QDMAP.** They are answering different questions and are both legitimate; conflating them is the error. ΔAIC is a penalty comparison *within one likelihood*, on a fixed dataset, for two nested models, and it is a statement about fit quality per parameter. QDMAP (Knox & Millea, 2202.12214) is a profile-likelihood construction aimed at the *unbiasedness* of H_0, designed so that the CMB-inferred H_0 is invariant to adding data that should not move it. So: a model can win on ΔAIC and lose on QDMAP, and that is informative rather than paradoxical — it means the extra flexibility bought H_0 by moving the likelihood in a direction the QDMAP axis is built to penalise. Two cautions I will attach to early_a's use. First, Ruling 4's caveat is not a footnote: r_s h = 101.8 ± 1.3 Mpc is DESI-induced in a fit that *contains* SH0ES, so the axis is partly constrained by the very sample it is being used to test. Second, 2310.16800's own numbers say the same thing in the early direction: ΔAIC(EDE − ADE) = **+7.3**, i.e. EDE is *worse* than ADE by AIC on the paper's own dataset. The paper is candid that its 2.8σ CPL preference is a fit to the *shape* of H_0(z) and is highly sensitive to the SN sample. Any panel statement should say "alleviates on QDMAP, penalised on ΔAIC" rather than picking one.

II), with Ω_bh² = 0.02237 fixed from Planck and the CMB again entering only as a 2×2 Gaussian distance prior. # Consensus Statement of the Cosmology Workshop Panel

## Session 1: The Hubble Tension

**Submitted to the Programme Committee, in response to the final call of this session.**
**Certified by:** the panel judge, acting on the transcript at `debate/TRANSCRIPT.md`.
**State certified:** Round 1 open at **4 of 5 panelists posted**; the statistician (methods) has not spoken. The gaps this leaves are named in §6. Nothing in this document pretends to a unanimity the panel did not reach.

---

## 1. The question, and what the panel was asked to settle

The session was asked whether the discrepancy between the Planck-inferred value of the Hubble constant (H₀ ≈ 67.4 ± 0.5 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹) and the SH0ES Cepheid-calibrated value (H₀ ≈ 73.04 ± 1.04 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹) — a gap of 5.6 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, **8.4σ** — is evidence of new physics, of a systematic in the measurement, or of both.

The panel's answer, which is the one thing all four positions turned out to share, is that **the question as posed cannot be answered by picking a side, because every candidate resolution on the table can be priced.** §2 states the price list. It is the panel's principal finding and the spine of this statement.

A prior commitment, made at the outset of the session, was honoured without exception: the panel would not write "solves," "resolves" or "reconciles" for any candidate. The verb the panel uses is **"reduces."** No candidate in the archive reduces the tension to below 2σ in a fit that does not contain the quantity being disputed.

---

## 2. The panel's principal finding: the payment table

Across nine distinct papers the panel found a single common structure. **Not one resolution moves H₀ without paying somewhere that is not H₀.** The payments are, in each case, measurable and, in most cases, already measured.

| What the H₀ is bought with | By whom | The price, measured |
|---|---|---|
| **n_s** | axion-like EDE (2008.01115) | n_s 0.9873 → 0.9724^{+0.0030}_{−0.0032}; with the SD test, H₀ 71.2 → 69.41^{+0.63}_{−0.75} |
| **n_s, again** | DRMD / dark drag horizon (2602.23895) | n_s 0.9646 → 0.9674 (0.45σ, CMB only) → **0.9778 (2.09σ)**; the extra 0.0104 is added by the SN-calibrated sample |
| **complexity, against the fit** | six HDE models (2511.09467) | OHDE H₀ = 71.44, 1.74σ — at **ΔBIC = +30.01**, with χ²_min rising 16.22 → 43.93 |
| **Ω_m** | HDE / acoustic EDE | Ω_m = 0.2731 ± 0.0022, **3.4σ below Pantheon+**; acoustic EDE 1.8σ, QDMAP 3.6σ |
| **a hard splice in expansion history** | GPAge mid-time (2608.28260) | E is discontinuous at z_cr unless the two H₀ agree; H₀,EU driven to 22.7–25.7 in CMB fits |
| **a fixed parameter** | PAge void fits (2504.13380) | ΔBIC = −73.28 obtained with the void parameters held at 20σ outliers |
| **sample variance** | the 150–300 Mpc local void | 20σ short; the paper's own second case gives only 2.5% of the gap, the first 1.0% |
| **an unidentified zero-point error** | the measurement position | **0.16–0.17 mag** on the Cepheid first rung, against a *known, named, unretired* photometric term of 1.4–1.8% in distance |
| **three transitions in SN magnitude** | ΛLTB + M-transition | transitions at ~20, ~129, ~860–960 Mpc; no mechanism proposed for any of the three |
| **nothing measurable, yet** | ΛLTB + 0.346 transition | predicted δ_M = 0.0730 ± 0.0031; measured 0.0461 ± 0.0066 — **3.3σ**, and the discrepancy is unexplained |

The last row is the panel's summary of the first nine. A resolution whose predicted observable has not been found, and whose found observable disagrees, has not reduced the tension; it has relocated it.

This is the finding.** The paper's own "null case" — helium-4, deuterium and helium-3, **lithium excluded** — returns Δα/α = 4.6 ± 3.8 ppm (unification), 3.7 ± 8.4 (dilaton), 0.8^{+1.5}_{−0.6} (clocks) with priors: **all consistent with zero.** The abstract says it plainly: "if this is excluded from the analysis, then within the statistical uncertainties, the standard values are recovered throughout." So varying α is not a resolution of *something*; it is a re-parametrisation of the lithium datum. **My standing diagnostic from session 1 applies unchanged, and it is the test I ask the panel to adopt for this session: a proposal whose signal disappears entirely when one measurement is removed has not identified a mechanism, it has identified a residual.** I make this a general rule of the session, because the same structure recurs: it is exactly the shape of "the void model works only with the CMB in the fit" and "EDE works only with DESI in the fit."

**3. Where the price lands — the session-1 axis, Ruling 15, reproduced here in a new field.** Allow η and N_ν to vary and the lithium problem does not go away; it *converts* into a tension in a parameter measured elsewhere. Without priors, baseline: unification prefers **η₁₀ = 6.79 ± 0.35** against Planck's **6.104 ± 0.058** — **1.93σ** high; dilaton prefers **N_ν = 1.86 ± 0.43** against LEP's **2.984 ± 0.008** — **2.61σ** low, which the paper itself calls "in obvious conflict with the LEP result"; clocks prefers **η₁₀ = 6.6 ± 0.2**, **2.38σ** from Planck. Allow the neutron lifetime to vary and the paper's own words: the abundances prefer "even as low as 812 seconds in the case of the dilaton model" (best fit **811.4 ± 28.7 s**), "excluded by the aforementioned experiments at well over two standard deviations" (**2.37σ** from 879.5 ± 0.8; unification 840.8 ± 26.9, 1.44σ). **So the new-physics answer to lithium buys a 10.4σ astrophysical tension at the cost of a 1.9–2.6σ tension in a *locally measured* quantity, or a 2.4σ tension in a laboratory neutron lifetime.** That is the same trade as Round 1 — n_s, Ω_m, fit quality, a fixed parameter, sample variance — and it is the strongest reason the panel's cross-session statement should be about *where a resolution pays* rather than about which resolution wins.

**4. The paper contradicts its own abstract, and the contradiction kills two of its three models.** The abstract claims: "By excluding lithium from the analysis, we also obtain upper limits... |Δα/α| < 50 ppm without... priors, or alternatively **|Δα/α| < 5 ppm if these priors are used**." But its Table 7, with the LEP and Planck priors *in use*, reports baseline best fits of **Δα/α = 16.1 ± 3.9 ppm (unification) and 22.6 ± 5.5 ppm (dilaton)**. Those are **2.85σ and 3.20σ above the paper's own 5 ppm limit.** Applying the abstract's limit to its own solutions excludes the two specific GUT models the paper offers as solutions. The only survivor is the **clocks** model — the one with R and S marginalised over a five-dimensional space, R ≈ 40, S ≈ 100 — at **Δα/α = 2.5^{+2.5}_{−0.5} ppm**, whose upper 1σ reaches 5.0 and whose upper 2σ reaches 7.5. **A solution that survives only in the most flexible, most prior-dependent corner, at a significance the authors themselves describe as "a very asymmetric (and obviously non-Gaussian) posterior likelihood," is not a detection.** The model spread with priors is a factor of **9** (22.6 vs 2.5) across three choices of the same physics — which is what "model-dependent" means quantitatively, and the paper says so itself in its conclusions. **Report the spread, not the member of the family that flatters the question.**

**5. The deuterium trade, which the paper raises against everyone else and its own coefficients confirm.** The introduction flags "the cost of overproducing deuterium... the two abundances are anticorrelated," and Table 1's sensitivity coefficients are the mechanism: **C_7Li = x_i + y_i S + z_i R = −166.6 − 151.6 S − 200.9 R** against **C_D = 42.0 + 39.2 S + 36.6 R.** In the clocks best fit (R ≈ 40, S ≈ 100) these are **−23,363 vs +5,426**, a ratio of **−0.232**: every 1 ppm of α lowers lithium by 2.34% and raises D by 0.54%. And D is *already* on the wrong side — observed 2.545 ± 0.025 against predicted 2.459 ± 0.036, **1.96σ high**. **The proposed remedy therefore spends lithium against a deuterium discrepancy that already exists, and the D data are one of the three nuclides it fits.** This is a real, quantified cost the headline does not mention, and I ask the panel to record it. The honest counterpoint, which the paper itself makes: the extremely iron-poor dwarf lithium abundances are "very close to" the Spite plateau (Aguado et al. 2019), which is the strongest single evidence *against* the depletion branch and the main reason a new-physics branch is on the table at all. That is why I am testing the varying-α branch rather than dismissing it.

**6. What the panel cannot yet do, and my one request.** Session 2 asks new physics against stellar depletion and nuclear rates. The archive contains **one** paper, on one side. I cannot test the other side at all: there is no nuclear-rate paper here (so the Iliadis & Coc route the paper cites — "steady improvements in experimental techniques have all but closed this possible loophole" — is unverified) and no depletion paper (so Ryan et al.'s factor-1.8 depletion and the Spite plateau cannot be weighed). **My request to the chair: assign 2012.10505 formally, and do not let a single-sided archive produce a verdict.** I will apply the same four-question test to whatever arrives, and the second question I will press is the one this paper invites: **is the price measurable and quoted by the proposer?** By that standard this paper does well on honesty — it publishes its null case, its model spread, and its conflicts with LEP — and badly on self-consistency, because the 5 ppm limit and the 16–23 ppm solutions cannot both stand.

**Position.** 2012.10505 is a *mechanism with a bookkept price*, not a resolution. Its signal is entirely lithium-borne (null case recovers zero), its price lands in η₁₀ at 1.93σ and N_ν at 2.61σ or in τ_n at 2.37σ, it overproduces deuterium at 0.54% per ppm against a 1.96σ D discrepancy, and two of its three models are excluded by its own abstract's 5 ppm limit at 2.85σ and 3.20σ. The verb remains **"reduces."** And the panel's lithium statement cannot be written from this archive.

11: ABSTRACT
12: The success of primordial nucleosynthesis has been limited by the long-standing Lithium problem. We use a self-consistent per-
13: turbative analysis of the eﬀects of relevant theoretical parameters on primordial nucleosynthesis, including variations of nature’s
14: fundamental constants, to explore the problem and its possible solutions, in the context of the latest observations and theoretical
15: modeling. We quantify the amount of depletion needed to solve the Lithium problem, and show that transport processes of chemical
16: elements in stars are able to account for it. Speciﬁcally, the combination of atomic diﬀusion, rotation and penetrative convection
17: allows us to reproduce the lithium surface abundances of Population II stars, starting from the primordial Lithium abundance. We also
18: show that even with this depletion factor there is a preference for a value of the ﬁne-structure constant at this epoch that is larger than
19: the current laboratory one by a few parts per million of relative variation, at the two to three standard deviations level of statistical
20: signiﬁcance. This preference is driven by the recently noticed discrepancy between the best-ﬁt values for the baryon-to-photon ratio
21: (or equivalently the Deuterium abundance) inferred from cosmic microwave background and primordial nucleosynthesis analyses,
22: and is largely insensitive to the Helium-4 abundance. We thus conclude that the Lithium problem most likely has an astrophysical
23: solution, while the Deuterium discrepancy provides a possible hint of new physics.
